Saskatoon transit implementing a free child fair. We have a speaker on this, but first we'll hear from administration.
Thank you Mr. Chair and my introduction is a little longer than typical today because there's just a lot of information in this report I would like to summarize.
Saskatoon Transit will begin offering free fair for children on September 1st, 2024 on public transit and access transit to provide a low cost transportation option for families.
This report provides recommendations for applicable age and verification for the free child fair.

To inform these recommendations, stakeholder engagement was undertaken between February and March 2024 to assist Saskatoon Transit in determining how best to design and implement an effective program that meets a community's needs and improve the accessibility and affordability.

And affordability of public transit engagement activities included a benchmark survey with Canadian transit agencies feedback from Regina transit meetings and surveys with the Saskatoon public schools and greater Saskatoon Catholic schools engagement sessions and survey with Saskatoon transit employees engagement with ATU local 615 and with the bus riders of Saskatoon facilitated sessions and a survey for community groups and an online public survey.
Participants in all engagement activities identified that grade 8 and under was a highest ranked option for eligibility for free child fair.
The ATU local 615 agreed that grade is appropriate for determining eligibility rather than age.

The community groups and discussions at in-person sessions along with 75% of elementary schools 62% of residents who participated in the public survey and the bus riders of Saskatoon prefer that children not be required to scan a pass.
Or provide identification of age when boarding the bus.
These groups preferred no pass, adult, accompaniment, or proof of age to be required to board to reduce barriers and make it easy for everyone to use.
Additional community groups not present at the in-person sessions who took the survey were split on whether verification method was necessary or not.

ATU local 615 says expressed to city council and to the administration that the preference of operators is that the city require a child pass or similar method to assist operators with age verification for children.

Noting concerns that for each child fair will become an opportunity for teens and adults to exploit the fair policy which could worse in the problem and lead to more fair disputes with frontline transit workers.

The top concerns with reach out fair from Saskatoon Transit employee survey were the safety of unaccompanied younger children increased disruptive incidents with groups of older children on the bus and more fair disputes with adults and high school students.
The Canadian Urban Transit Association or QDAC coordinated a benchmark survey on behalf of Saskatoon Transit responses were submitted by 15 transit agencies.
93% of those who completed the survey have reached out fair mostly for those 12 years and under.
Of those 71% rely on the child to self identify with no pass or verification.
While half are not experiencing issues the other half reported an increase in fair vision among teens and adults.
Regina Transit has free bus fair for children 13 and under who self identify when boarding.
The administration and transient union representatives through separate surveys identified an increase in fair vision and older children on buses.
Two options were considered for applicable age option one a children in grade eight and under right free and option one b children 13 years and under right free.
Administration is recommending option one a for the following reasons survey respondents for all groups preferred this eligibility criteria.
It aligns with current eligibility for the child pass which reduces the impact on other fair products for current writers and all elementary school children will be eligible for free child fair.

Three options were considered for verification of child fair option to a which children would self verify to right free option to be children right free with a child pass and option to see children right free when accompanied by an adult.

The administration sees option to a and to be as equally ranked options option to a is recommended primarily because the majority of the groups and people involved with the public engagement preferred having no age verification.

That could present barriers for children to participate in this program further this approach makes public transit affordable and fully accessible for families which is what the community groups schools and residents preferred.
Occasional and spontaneous writers and families would have easy access when they take public transit.
As for next step Saskatoon Transit will develop an extensive advertising campaign to promote the program throughout the summer up to September 1st launch.

The communicates and strategy will use school and community partner channels to encourage families to subscribe for email updates on free child fair before school lets out in June for updates throughout the summer.
The first email will update all survey participants who shared their email addresses with the survey results and the final program eligibility.
The website and other fair products will be updated as quickly as possible.
The intent of implementing free child fair in September 2024 was to have no impact on Saskatoon Transit's 2024 revenue budget.
If there is an impact in 2024, it will be reported back for future budget deliberations.

The report that I'm presenting this afternoon is regarding the annual taxi fair review.
To ensure consistent pricing, taxi fairs are regulated in the vehicle for higher by law.
Administration completes a taxi cost index review annually, which compares operating cost to providing taxi service over the previous 24 months, compared to a base rate set in 2011.
This ensures that over time, taxi fairs can be adjusted to keep up with any increased operating cost, such as fuel vehicle prices,
maintenance and insurance.
A taxi cost index was completed in May 2023, which shows that cost had increased by 11% since fairs were last increased in 2020.
Administration recommended addressing the fair increase in two parts.
The first part was an increase to the minimum starting fair from $3.75 to $4.75.
This would increase the total fair of a five-kilometer trip by approximately 7%.
City Council adopted this amendment in June 2023.
The second part was an increase to the distance rate.
This report addresses the second phase of the increase, and recommends increasing the distance rate from 25 cents for every 117 meters to 25 cents for every 110 meters.
This amount is equivalent to approximately a five percent increase in the total fair for a five-kilometer trip.
A proportionate increase to the hourly rate is also recommended.
Administration arrived at this amount through an analysis of the taxi cost index, which considered operating costs for the period of March 2022 to February 2024,
and found that operating costs set increased by 10% over this period.
Administration also conducted a municipal scan and found that Saskatoon's current taxi fairs were the fourth highest of cities on the scan,
and exceeded those of Regina, Calgary, Winnipeg, and Edmonton.
Increasing fairs by a further 10% would result in Saskatoon having the second highest fairs.
Administration engaged with leaders in the taxi industry, including taxi brokers, and the union that represents most drivers,
and shared the results of the index and the scan.
Engagement participants unanimously agreed that a five percent increase in fairs was appropriate,
as it would enable a moderate increase to the distance rate while maintaining Saskatoon's current position in the municipal scan.

Fixed route service average cost per passenger decrease by 63 cents in 2023 due to increased ridership and operational savings.
Access transit had a surplus of $396,000 at the end of 2023. In 2022, there were in 2023, there was an increase in demand of 18%.
The average meal rate, a support cost per trip for access transit decreased by 90 cents in 2023 due to increased ridership and operational savings.
